as_of.graph_vintage: kuzu_nessie_db built 2026-08-30T01:51:34Z (27,073 nodes / 60,552 edges) for the AWS-plane trigger sweep. The cse table's own row counts are NOT read by this card -- they are a run-time retrieval, see coverage.

methodology.how: A one-shot orchestrator run as a Fargate task on the derive image. It loads the Nessie catalog, ensures the cse table, reads the CURRENT event_id set as a dedup spine, then runs three env-gated producer legs in sequence, each in its own try/except with its own import so one leg failing (or missing from the image) never blocks the others. Every leg filters its built batch against the existing event_ids before appending, so a re-run appends 0 -- IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a separate backfill script. Count-before and count-after are read back FROM THE CATALOG and printed every run; the writer never reports its own append count as the truth.

stages_inferential: leg_agent: a recognizer over recent s3://opal-mcp-audit/audit/ keys behind a SAFE_TOOLS allowlist -- a classification step, and the only leg whose output is not a direct projection. Default-DISABLED (CSE_AGENT_ENABLED=0).
stages_deterministic: leg_graphhead: build_graph_head_cses at full scope behind the dedup filter -- a projection of the graph
leg_sweep: ingest of already-built JSONL batches from the pending prefix
the dedup filter itself: set membership on event_id

composes.note: catalog, table ensure, SNAPSHOT_BUCKET and stamp_marker
the append target AND the dedup source -- read before write, every run

invents.note: CSE_GRAPHHEAD_ENABLED / CSE_SWEEP_ENABLED / CSE_AGENT_ENABLED, so the option ruling is a task-def env flip rather than a code change
the standing lane for LOCAL-source producers whose repo/git sources a Fargate task cannot see

coverage.universe: CSE events appendable to iceberg.globgrph.cse from the three producer legs: graph_head at full graph scope, the staged JSONL batches in the pending prefix, and (when enabled) the agent recognizer over recent audit keys.
coverage.denominator_absent_reason: THE DENOMINATOR IS A RUN-TIME RETRIEVAL AND THIS CARD DID NOT RUN IT. existing_event_ids() :106-114 reads the live table and prints 'CSE_LOG_BEFORE rows=<n> distinct_event_ids=<m>' -- that pair IS the run's retrieval denominator, and the docstring names it as such. Stating a number here would require executing the writer against the live Nessie catalog, which is in-VPC only and out of scope for a carding read. The docstring's one quoted figure -- the C0 spine 'static at 342 since the 07-09 SEMCTL close' -- is the SPINE's size, not this writer's output cardinality, and reporting it as the latter would be a grain substitution.

Anything a Fargate task cannot see: the LOCAL-source producers (deploy / frontend_coevolution / promote / agent local emits) reach the table only via the pending-prefix sweep, never directly.

key.identity_space: Producer-minted CSE event ids in a single flat namespace, shared by all three legs and by the LOCAL-source producers that stage batches.
key.key_expression: `event_id`, a column on iceberg.globgrph.cse. Producers mint it structurally rather than randomly: the graph_head leg's ids are 'graph_head:node:{nid}' and 'graph_head:edge:{...}' (docstring :20). A consumer computes membership by set-inclusion on that column -- which is exactly what the writer itself does at :106-114 before every append.
key.evidence: MEASURED at source and, unusually, EXERCISED BY THE SUBJECT ITSELF: the key expression is not merely declared, it is the writer's own idempotency spine. existing_event_ids() :106-114 scans the table for event_id only and returns the distinct set; filter_new() :116-127 splits every built batch on membership in that set. key_is_stable 'stable' is measured from the same code path rather than assumed: the docstring states 'stable producer event_ids + append-only writer => a re-run appends 0', and filter_new's within-batch collapse comment ('last wins -- producer event_ids are stable, the payload is equivalent') is the author asserting stability as the property the dedup depends on. crosses_spaces FALSE: one namespace, no join to a second identity space, so declared_mapping is null with basis measured -- there is nothing to map, and that is a measured fact rather than a missing one.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: MOSTLY FAIL-CLOSED, WITH ONE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION. The idempotency spine is hard-gated: if existing_event_ids() raises, run() prints 'ERROR: DEDUP_SNAPSHOT_FAIL ... refusing to run any leg without the idempotency spine (an unfiltered append is the duplicate class)' and no leg executes -- the writer will not append rather than append unfiltered. A malformed staged batch is MOVED to rejected/ with an ERROR rather than retried forever. Per-leg failures are caught, named, and set rc=1 while the other legs still run. THE EXCEPTION: the snapshot guard on graph_nodes/graph_edges prints 'WARN: SNAPSHOT_GUARD_VERDICT' and does NOT fail the run -- a concurrent incremental_updater commit is DISCLOSED, not blocked.
silent_degrade_paths: THE SNAPSHOT GUARD IS A WARN, NOT A GATE. If a graph table's snapshot_id moves during a run, the verdict line says WARN and the task still exits 0 (rc is set by failed LEGS only, :358). The docstring frames this as 'disclosed, not masked' and that is honest -- but a consumer reading only the ECS task state sees success, and the disclosure lives in a CloudWatch log line nothing consumes.

A DISABLED LEG AND A FAILED-TO-IMPORT LEG ARE BOTH SILENT IN THE SAME PLACE. Legs are env-gated and each imports inside its own try/except, so a leg missing from the image produces the same 'this leg contributed nothing' shape as a leg deliberately switched off. The rc distinguishes them (rc=1 only if an ENABLED leg hard-failed), but the append count does not.

stamp_marker is best-effort and never unwinds a landed Nessie commit, so an append can land with no marker -- a downstream freshness reader keyed to the marker sees staleness that the table does not have.
TWIN_HEARTBEAT_FAIL prints ERROR but does not change rc, so the absence twin can go unwritten on an otherwise successful run.
failure_mode.evidence: All read at source: DEDUP_SNAPSHOT_FAIL :297-300; the rejected-batch arm :199-201; the per-leg try/except and failed-list :309-311; the terminal 'return 1 if failed else 0' :358; SNAPSHOT_GUARD_VERDICT's OK/WARN ternary at :323-324; stamp_marker :317 with the docstring's best-effort clause :33-34; TWIN_HEARTBEAT_FAIL :350-351. 'distinguishable_from_true_negative: yes' is measured on the PRIMARY failure -- an unfiltered append cannot happen quietly because the dedup gate refuses the whole run -- and the four degrade paths above are the honest qualification on that yes, each one named rather than folded into it.

verdict.why: One of the better-built writers in this population: idempotent by construction rather than by a separate backfill path, grounded on the live store rather than on its own report, fail-closed on the one condition that would cause duplicate appends, and carrying a snapshot guard specifically to prove it did not touch tables it has no business touching. Three qualifications. (1) SIX WRITE PATHS, ONE NAMED IN THE MANIFEST -- the table append, done/, rejected/, two heartbeat objects and the marker; a file-grain census undercounts this writer's surfaces by five. (2) THE SNAPSHOT GUARD IS A WARN, NOT A GATE: it discloses but does not block, and the disclosure lands in a log line nothing consumes while the task still exits 0. (3) live_matches_declared is unmeasured -- I read that the SCHEDULE exists and is DECLARED, not that it has been firing, so DESIRED is measured and APPLIED is not.
